title: Цветы от тайного поклонника и допрос Кости  (Flowers from a Secret Admirer and Questioning Kostya)

segments.t: When Elena calls Chef Barinov on the phone to thank him warmly for the anonymous bouquet of flowers, Barinov realizes his gesture worked after all. Meanwhile at the apartment, Nastya eagerly questions a nervous Kostya about whether he spoke with her father and if her parents are coming tomorrow.
Хотел сказать вам огромное спасибо за цветы.
Костик, ну что, не молчи, говори.
Now let's go back through the conversation line by line.
'Hello, Viktor Petrovich, good afternoon.' Notice how Russian expresses 'hello' and 'day' with crisp inflection rather than helper words. Chef Viktor answers right away.
'Hello. Yes, hello.' Chef Viktor anchors the line on 'hello', while 'hello' completes the thought.
Хотел сказать вам огромное спасибо за цветы.
'I wanted to say a huge thank-you for the flowers.' The '-l' ending on the verb meaning 'wanted' places the action in the masculine past tense.
'You are always welcome for the flowers.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'always' before landing on 'flowers'. Chef Viktor answers right away.
'How did you find out they were from me?' In Russian, the idea of 'where from' flows naturally into 'found out' without extra filler words.
'Well, how could I not?' Vika anchors the line on 'come on', while 'how' completes the thought.
'Just like you.' Max chooses the respectful plural 'you' alongside 'you' to keep a polite distance. Chef Viktor answers right away.
'Thank you so very much once again.' The grammar packs 'else' and 'thank you' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
'Well, did you talk to my dad?' In Russian, the idea of 'come on' flows naturally into 'dad' without extra filler words.
'And what did you say to him?' Notice how Russian expresses 'both' and 'to say' with crisp inflection rather than helper words. Chef Viktor answers right away.
'Did he speak politely with you?' In Russian, the idea of 'he' flows naturally into 'you' without extra filler words.
'Are they coming over to our place tomorrow?' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'they' before landing on 'tomorrow'.
Костик, ну что, не молчи, говори.
'Kostik, come on, do not stay silent, tell me.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'Kostik' and finishing on 'say'. Alright, let's hear the whole conversation once more from start to finish.
Хотел сказать вам огромное спасибо за цветы.
Костик, ну что, не молчи, говори.
